For deeper reading, inspect how reasoning coverage is operationalized, which held-out capabilities are used, and whether the claim that required population size decreases with model scale holds consistently across model families.50:T91c,RubricRM is a pairwise generative reward model. The input is an instruction q and two candidate images I_A and I_B; image editing additionally includes a source image. Instead of directly predicting which image is better, the model generates a structured rubric and dimension-level assessments for both candidates in one pass. The rubric includes task intent, atomic evaluation dimensions d_i, weights w_i over those dimensions, and scoring criteria L_i for each dimension. The model then assigns per-dimension scores s_i^k to each image, aggregates them with the learned weights, and derives the final preference from the weighted totals.

The key design choice is not merely to produce free-form rationales, but to turn explanation into a structured scoring protocol. That makes the output more controllable and allows training signals to operate at the dimension level rather than only at the final pairwise label.

Training has two stages. In the SFT stage, the model learns rubric trajectories synthesized by a teacher: how to decompose the instruction into intent, dimensions, weights, criteria, and then score the candidates. In the RL stage, the paper uses dimension-level GRPO. The objective aligns predicted score differences with reference score differences on each rubric dimension, and penalizes preference-direction reversals more strongly. This indicates that the authors care not only about final pairwise accuracy but also about the internal correctness of the dimension-wise judgment process.

Data construction is a major part of the contribution. The paper argues that dynamic rubric learning requires broad instruction coverage; otherwise the model will learn biased rubric templates and generalize poorly. To address this, the authors aggregate multiple open-source preference datasets, analyze instruction types for text-to-image generation and image editing, define classification criteria, and use DeepSeek-V3.2 for automatic taxonomy annotation. They then perform balanced sampling, identify underrepresented categories, synthesize additional prompts for those categories, generate candidate images, collect expert preference annotations, and finally synthesize rubric trajectories for each preference sample. The resulting training sets contain 31.8K text-to-image samples and 30.7K image-editing samples.51:T54f,The experiments train dedicated models for text-to-image generation and image editing on Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3.5-9B backbones. The headline numbers reported in the text are: RubricRM-Gen-9B reaches 72.00 on MMRB2, 74.12 on GenAI-Bench, and 84.45 on GenAI-Bench-Verified; RubricRM-Edit-9B reaches 75.40 on MMRB2, 46.40 on EditReward-ERB, and 85.64 on EditScore-ERB. The paper states that these results outperform existing reward-model baselines across both generation and editing.

The most informative parts of the experimental section are likely not just the main table, but three kinds of analysis: (1) the effect of the two-stage pipeline—SFT only, preference optimization only, and SFT plus GRPO; (2) the effect of data coverage—whether balanced sampling and long-tail supplementation improve generalization on underrepresented instruction types; and (3) the value of the rubric structure itself—how much is lost when replacing dynamic rubrics with fixed criteria or a plain scalar preference head.

If deciding whether to follow up, check two things first: the gain over fixed-dimension reward models, and whether dimension-level RL actually improves final pairwise preference accuracy.53:T8c1,方法设计很克制，核心是“保留标准 student update，只在严格筛选的条件下做 student-to-teacher adaptation”。训练仍然从 student on-policy rollout 开始：student 只看题目 x 采样解答 y，teacher 在同一条 partial rollout 上、但额外看到参考解 y*，输出逐 token 分布。标准 OPSD 部分不变，student 继续用 teacher 的 token-level target 做蒸馏更新。VISTA 新增的是 teacher 更新，而且只在两层筛选后发生。

第一层是 rollout-level gating。只有当 student rollout 通过 outcome verifier 时，这条 rollout 才被认为包含了值得 teacher 学习的 problem-only reasoning 轨迹。这里的判断不是“student 比 teacher 强”，而是“这条 rollout 至少在结果上成立，因此其中某些 student token 偏好可能比 reference-conditioned teacher 更贴近部署时可行的推理分布”。这样做避免把 teacher 拉向明显错误的 student 行为。

第二层是 token-level selection。即便 rollout 最终正确，也不意味着整条序列的每个位置都该拿来更新 teacher。论文用 teacher-student disagreement 的 KL 信号做位置选择，只在 top-k 个分歧最大的 token 位置上，把 teacher 向 student 适度拉近。这里的直觉很重要：真正需要修正的是 teacher 最不贴近 problem-only reasoning 的位置，而不是所有位置。若全序列都更新，teacher 很快会塌缩到 student，失去 privileged knowledge，后续也就无法继续提供互补监督。

从损失形式看，VISTA 复用了标准 OPSD 的同类蒸馏损失，没有再造一个复杂目标。它的创新不在 loss 公式本身，而在“哪些 rollout 能作为 teacher 反馈”“哪些 token 位置值得反馈”这两个选择机制。论文还把这一设计与已有方法区分得比较清楚：RLSD 是在 student 侧用 verifier reward 约束更新方向；TRACE 是限制 distillation 的 token span；DemoPSD 是在 teacher-student disagreement 时重加权 student target。它们都在减少 student 受坏 teacher 影响，但 teacher 本身仍是静态的。VISTA 则让 teacher 在受控条件下被 student 的成功行为校准，因此改变的是监督源本身。54:T4a5,The main significance is conceptual and methodological. Conceptually, the paper reframes privileged distillation as a target-alignment problem rather than a simple stronger-model-supervises-weaker-model setup. That matters beyond reasoning post-training. Any setting with a conditioning gap between teacher and student—reference-conditioned teachers, tool-augmented teachers, retrieval-conditioned teachers, multimodal teachers supervising text-only students—faces the same issue. Methodologically, VISTA introduces a controlled feedback loop from student to teacher without discarding the standard OPSD student update. This is a meaningful contribution because it changes the supervision source itself, not just the student's robustness to bad supervision. Empirically, the gains are consistent across three Qwen3 scales, and the method stays lightweight: no extra sampling and no separate RL objective. For researchers working on pretrain/post-train interfaces, the useful lesson is that supervision quality depends not only on teacher capability, but also on whether the teacher distribution is calibrated to the student's observable information and feasible reasoning trajectories.55:T9b5,VISTA keeps the standard OPSD pipeline intact and adds a tightly controlled student-to-teacher adaptation step. Training still begins with an on-policy student rollout: the student policy sees only the problem x and samples a solution y, while the teacher sees both x and the reference solution y*. Both models are evaluated on the same partial student rollout. The student update remains unchanged: it is still distilled toward the teacher's token-level distribution, exactly as in standard OPSD.

The new part is the teacher update, and it is gated twice.

First, VISTA applies rollout-level selection using an outcome verifier. Only student rollouts that pass verification are allowed to provide feedback to the teacher. The logic is not that the student is globally better than the teacher, but that a verified rollout contains evidence that some of the student's token-level preferences are compatible with successful problem-only reasoning. This prevents the teacher from being pulled toward clearly bad student behavior.

Second, VISTA applies token-level selection within each eligible rollout. Even a correct rollout should not be used wholesale. The paper computes teacher-student disagreement and selects the top-k positions with the largest KL discrepancy. Teacher adaptation is applied only at those sparse positions. This is the central design choice. The goal is to correct the teacher exactly where its distribution is most misaligned with successful problem-only reasoning, while preserving the rest of the teacher's privileged knowledge. If the teacher were updated densely across all positions, the teacher-student gap would collapse too quickly and the teacher would lose its complementary value as a privileged supervisor.

An important practical point is that VISTA reuses the same rollouts and the same family of distillation losses as standard OPSD. The novelty is not a new reward function or a complicated optimization objective. It lies in deciding which rollouts are trustworthy for teacher feedback and which token positions are worth adapting. This also distinguishes VISTA from prior methods. RLSD constrains student updates with verifier rewards; TRACE restricts distillation to selected spans; DemoPSD reweights the target toward the student when teacher and student disagree. All of them reduce student exposure to mismatched teacher targets, but the teacher remains static. VISTA instead calibrates the teacher itself using verified student behavior.56:T83a,The main experiments cover three Qwen3 model scales—1.7B, 4B, and 8B—on three competition-math benchmarks under a matched OPSD protocol. The headline result is straightforward: VISTA achieves the best Avg@12 average across the three benchmarks at all three scales. Relative to reported OPSD, the average improves by 0.6, 0.7, and 2.1 points at 1.7B, 4B, and 8B respectively. The largest gain appears at 8B, which suggests that teacher adaptation may become more valuable as model capability increases. Across the nine scale-benchmark combinations, VISTA is best in eight.

The ablations are more informative than the topline numbers. Removing verifier-gated rollout selection hurts performance, indicating that teacher adaptation cannot be safely driven by arbitrary student trajectories. Removing selective top-k position adaptation and updating the teacher more broadly also degrades results, which supports the paper's core claim: the benefit does not come from making the teacher more student-like everywhere, but from sparse correction at the most mismatched positions.

The analysis section appears to target the three failure modes identified in the introduction. First, the adapted teacher provides better support for validated student reasoning, meaning it assigns higher probability to successful problem-only continuations. Second, explicit reference attribution is reduced, which suggests less leakage from the teacher's privileged conditioning. Third, teacher capability is preserved, showing that sparse adaptation does not simply collapse the teacher into the student. These analyses matter because they connect the empirical gains back to the proposed mechanism rather than leaving the method as a black-box improvement.

The abstract does not expose every implementation detail, but the full paper is likely worth checking for the exact verifier setup, the top-k schedule, the distribution of teacher-student KL across positions, and how often teacher adaptation is applied. In causal patching, rotated English residuals often flip a target-language model’s factual cloze prediction to the donor capital, with the effect holding across five unrelated target languages and approaching the within-model patching ceiling.5b:T7b8,SCIT，Suffix Cache Interchange Test，本质上是一个 cache-level counterfactual intervention protocol。给定 recipient 问题 r 和 source 问题 s，先构造一个精确可验证的反事实：source 提供某个中间变量的替代值，把它与 recipient 其余变量组合后，得到已知正确的 counterfactual answer。然后让 latent-CoT 模型分别在 r 和 s 上 rollout 到某个 latent step t，在这个 patch 点把 source 的某个缓存切片插入 recipient，对比 recipient 的答案是否朝 source 定义的反事实移动。

方法不是只做一次 patch，而是做一整套 intervention grid。维度包括：patch 哪个 cache segment；只换 K、只换 V、还是 K/V 一起换；是否同时复制当前 hidden state；是否使用语义相近但答案相同的 source control；是否做 decoded validation，确认被 patch 的 latent 轨迹确实对应可读出的反事实行为；以及 matched corruption，用同一区域做破坏性干预来测试 necessity。作者据此定义三个状态：active carrier，指最小且 gated 的 cache segment，在 oracle interchange 下足够，并且主要竞争解释无法匹配；carrier shift，指存在可转移效应，但活跃片段与主结论模型不同；no-call，指由于能力、支持度、decoded 行为或控制检查不过关，不能下机制判断。

从全文看，论文最重要的技术细节有三点。第一，它强调 exact source-recipient counterfactual，而不是开放式 prompt patching，这样可以避免目标答案不明确。第二，它把 sufficiency 和 necessity 分开，且 necessity 通过 matched corruption 而不是随意噪声注入来做，减少“哪里都能破坏”的伪结论。第三，它把 hidden state 与 cache object 明确区分：h_t 不是 cache 的一部分，只有显式复制时才算干预对象。这让“是当前状态在算，还是历史 value 轨迹在承载”这个问题可以被单独检验。5c:T74d,SCIT, the Suffix Cache Interchange Test, is a cache-level counterfactual intervention protocol. For a recipient problem r and a source problem s, the method first constructs an exact, verifiable counterfactual: the source supplies a changed intermediate quantity, which is then combined with the recipient’s remaining variables to define a known counterfactual answer. Both source and recipient are rolled out to a latent step t. At that patch point, a selected cache slice from the source is transplanted into the recipient, optionally together with the current hidden state, and the test checks whether the recipient moves toward the source-defined counterfactual answer.

The protocol is deliberately grid-like rather than a single patch experiment. It varies: which cache segment is patched; whether only K, only V, or both are copied; whether the hidden state is also copied; whether semantic source controls with the same answer are used; whether decoded validation confirms that the patched latent trajectory corresponds to the intended counterfactual behavior; and whether matched corruption on the same region supports necessity. Based on this battery, the paper defines three outcomes: active carrier, carrier shift, and no-call.

Three technical choices are especially important. First, the paper uses exact source-recipient counterfactuals rather than open-ended prompt patching, which keeps the target answer unambiguous. Second, it separates sufficiency from necessity, and tests necessity with matched corruption rather than arbitrary noise, reducing the risk of overcalling mechanisms. Third, it explicitly distinguishes the current hidden state from the cache object: h_t is not part of the cache unless copied by intervention. That makes it possible to ask whether the computation is carried by the present state or by a historical value trajectory.5d:T6f0,The experiments are centered on controlled arithmetic settings, chosen because they allow exact counterfactual labels and clean negative controls. The main result is checkpoint-specific but strong: on the CODI-GPT2 arithmetic checkpoint, counterfactual answer transfer occurs primarily through value-cache suffix trajectories, with the strongest restricted effect in middle-to-late value segments. This region is not only sufficient under oracle interchange, but also supported by matched-corruption necessity, which is why the authors make a full mechanism call for a late-value-suffix carrier. In contrast, hidden-only transfer, key-only transfer, single-token triggers, same-answer semantic source controls, and partial-variable controls are all much weaker and do not explain the same effect.

On a Sim-CoT-style GPT-2 reproduction, the pattern is directionally similar: value-suffix sufficiency and decoded transfer are present, but matched-corruption necessity is not strong enough for a full necessity claim. The paper is explicit about that limitation.

A broader checkpoint sweep shows that the mechanism is not uniform. Some arithmetic-like GPT-2/1B cells preserve latent-tail value/KV transfer, while several competent 8B or repaired non-arithmetic cells shift the carrier to prompt-prefix or full-cache K/V. The authors call this a carrier shift rather than a replication of the CODI-GPT2 mechanism. Some cells are labeled no-call because competence gating, decoded behavior, support, or source-control checks fail. This is one of the paper’s strengths: it does not argue that latent CoT universally lives in value-cache suffixes; it provides a framework that can separate local mechanism evidence, regime shifts, and cases where no mechanism claim is justified.5e:T4bf,For a skim, focus on the protocol before the results. The introduction already states the scope clearly: the goal is not to prove a universal latent-CoT mechanism, but to define a carrier-test contract. Start with Figure 1 and the method section to understand the four-step flow: define the patch object, specify the intervention grid, validate the readout, and apply the carrier decision rule.

Then read how the arithmetic counterfactuals are constructed. That part explains why the source-recipient pairing is exact and why the protocol is not yet directly portable to open-domain reasoning tasks.

In the experiments, prioritize the CODI-GPT2 main result, because that is the only place where the paper claims a full sufficiency-plus-necessity mechanism. Then read the Sim-CoT-style checkpoint to see why it is treated as partial corroboration rather than full replication. Finally, inspect the carrier-regime map and pay attention to the gating logic behind active carrier, carrier shift, and no-call.

A 30-minute read is enough to capture the main idea. For a deeper pass, the appendix matters: intervention tables, prompt templates, and the full evaluation battery are where the paper earns its credibility.5f:T929,方法核心是一个 iterative prune-heal-backtrack 流程。模型被表示为 residual-stream writers/readers 构成的有向图：writer 包括 token embedding、每个 attention head 的 residual contribution、每个 MLP 输出；reader 包括后续 attention/MLP 输入以及最终 logits。边表示某个 writer 对下游 reader 的信息通路。与常见直接置零不同，作者采用 clean/corrupted prompt 配对，并在关闭边时用 corrupted prompt 上对应 writer 的 counterfactual activation 替代 clean activation，避免把读入分布推离数据流形。这样“边是否必要”更接近因果替换而不是粗暴破坏。

训练上只更新一个从零开始的 LoRA adapter，底座模型冻结。初始时所有边开放。每一轮先用因果重要性估计给当前存活边排序，然后剪掉一批最弱边；接着在新边掩码下训练 LoRA，使适配后的模型尽量复现原模型输出。这里的目标不是重新学任务标签，而是通过剩余通路逼近原模型 next-token distribution，因此它更像 constrained distillation。随后用 held-out controller 决定是否接受本轮剪枝：只有当目标行为准确率仍达标，且 off-target 语言建模能力没有明显恶化时，才保留这次删除，否则回退到上一状态。这个 accept/reject 机制很重要，因为它把“更小电路”约束在“行为保真 + 通用能力保真”之内，而不是单纯追求 sparsity。

作者把最终最小可接受电路记为 C1。与 frozen search 的区别在于：传统 EAP/EAP-IG/EAP-GP 之类方法只是在固定权重上估计边重要性；这里则允许通过低秩参数更新把行为迁移到更少边上。论文还专门做了一个对照：使用同样的搜索流程但不更新权重，结果明显更差，说明收益主要来自 reshaping behavior implementation，而不是搜索器本身更聪明。

另一个技术点是 fidelity 评估不只看任务准确率，还看与原模型输出分布的 KL，以及 condensed circuit 对原模型失败模式的预测能力。也就是说，作者知道“压缩后的小电路”可能只解释修改后的网络，因此专门测试它是否仍能描述原始未修改模型。这一点让方法不只是做出一个小模型，而是尽量保留对原模型机制的解释联系。60:T8f5,The method is an iterative prune-heal-backtrack procedure. A transformer is represented as a directed graph over residual-stream writers and readers. Writers include token embeddings, each attention head’s residual contribution, and each MLP output; readers include downstream attention/MLP inputs and final logits. Edges represent information flow from an upstream writer to a downstream reader.

A key design choice is how edges are ablated. Instead of zeroing an edge, the method uses paired clean/corrupted prompts and replaces the clean activation flowing through a closed edge with the corresponding activation from the corrupted prompt. This counterfactual replacement avoids pushing activations off-manifold, making edge necessity tests more causally meaningful than naive zero ablation.

Training updates only a freshly initialized LoRA adapter while keeping the base model frozen. Starting from all edges open, each round ranks surviving edges by causal importance, removes the weakest ones, and then trains the LoRA adapter to reproduce the original model’s outputs through the remaining graph. This is closer to constrained distillation than task finetuning: the goal is to match the original next-token distribution under a restricted internal pathway. A held-out controller then accepts the deletion only if both target-task accuracy and off-target language-modeling capability remain within tolerance; otherwise the method rolls back. The smallest accepted graph is denoted C1.

This differs sharply from frozen circuit search methods such as EAP-IG: those estimate importance under fixed weights, whereas Circuit Condensation allows low-rank adaptation to reshape where the behavior lives. The paper explicitly tests the same search loop without weight updates and finds that it loses badly, which isolates the gain to behavioral reshaping rather than better search alone.

Another strong point is the fidelity analysis. The authors do not stop at task accuracy on the adapted model. They also measure KL to the original model’s next-token distribution and test whether the condensed circuit predicts failure modes of the unmodified model better than size-matched frozen circuits. This is important because otherwise one could end up explaining only the modified network.61:T6f6,The evaluation spans 4 behaviors, 8 models from 4 families, and 3 random seeds. Candidate edge counts range from 2,041 in GPT-2 to 43,993 in Qwen3-4B. The headline result is that in 30 of 32 settings, C1 is smaller than the strongest frozen EAP-IG baseline at comparable task accuracy, by 8.1x on average and up to 316x. The sign test gives p = 2.5e-7, with a bootstrap interval of [4.9, 13.7]. Running the same search without weight updates loses in 29 of 32 settings, supporting the claim that the benefit comes from reshaping the implementation of the behavior.

The paper then shows why smaller circuits matter operationally. The condensed circuits make exhaustive subset tests, all-pairs ablations, and edge-level necessity checks feasible. Matched frozen circuits would require a median 55x more pairwise ablations, and subset enumeration is infeasible in all 19 matched cases reported. So the size reduction changes what verification questions can actually be computed.

On fidelity, the median KL to the original model’s next-token distribution is 0.215 across the grid, and 0.056 on the IOI anchor task, compared with 0.50 for a size-matched frozen circuit. The condensed circuits also better predict where the original model will fail than frozen circuits of the same size. That is a strong indication that the method is not merely producing a compact explanation for the adapted model, but retaining explanatory contact with the original one.

The paper also discusses limits: not every behavior condenses equally well, and some appear to resist concentration under capability constraints. Those failure cases are important because they speak to whether the method is exposing genuine redundancy or simply exploiting the flexibility of LoRA to rewrite local mechanisms.62:T4dd,For a quick read, focus on three things. First, read the introduction and the main method figure to internalize the objective: the paper is not trying to recover the one true frozen circuit, but to move a behavior into a smaller circuit under fidelity constraints. Second, read the sections defining edge gating, clean/corrupted activation replacement, LoRA-only healing, and the held-out accept/reject controller. Those choices are what make the method more than standard pruning. Third, inspect the results on circuit size, exhaustive verifiability, and fidelity to the original model.

If time is limited, Figure 1, the main comparison tables, and the sections on subset/pairwise verification plus the frozen-search ablation are the highest-yield parts. Around 30-40 minutes should be enough to get the main story. For deeper reading, pay attention to how the capability constraint is operationalized, how KL fidelity is measured, and how the failure cases are characterized. The two questions worth probing are whether condensation is distilling an existing mechanism or creating a new local implementation, and whether condensability depends on model scale, task type, or the degree of distributed representation learned during pretraining.63:T4be,Its value for foundation-model research is less about a new pretraining recipe and more about measurement at the pretrain/post-train boundary. Many alignment interventions—RLHF, DPO, SFT, refusal tuning, persona control, even retrieval-conditioned interaction—change how readily a model updates in multi-turn settings. If rational updating is not measured separately, training can easily turn “do not flatter the user” into “do not revise when new information arrives.” The contribution has three parts. First, it introduces a two-turn diagnostic that cleanly separates unsupported pressure from evidence-based revision. Second, it compares both training-time and inference-time interventions and shows that the trade-off is recurring rather than method-specific. Third, the mechanistic analysis suggests that the two behaviors share internal circuitry and aligned steering directions, which explains why naive suppression lacks selectivity. For anyone working on RLHF, DPO, SFT, activation steering, or agent systems that must incorporate external evidence, this is a useful warning: the intervention may be changing the model’s update threshold rather than improving truthfulness in a targeted way.64:T906,The method has three layers. The first is the evaluation design. The authors adapt four datasets—TruthfulQA, PopQA, EX-FEVER, and AQuA—into a two-turn setup. The model first answers the question on its own. In the second turn, it receives either a pressure message that merely challenges the answer without adding information, or an evidence message that supports the correct answer. This lets the authors measure answer revision under unsupported social pressure separately from revision under informative evidence. Formally, the object of study is the transition from the first-turn answer to the second-turn answer, conditioned on the type of feedback.

The second layer is intervention comparison. They evaluate four open-weight LLMs under representative anti-sycophancy interventions spanning both training-time and inference-time control, including SFT, DPO, and activation steering. The key is that they do not rely on single-turn accuracy. Instead, they track how each intervention changes Unsupported-Yielding and Rational-Updating in the two-turn setting. They also test joint optimization settings intended to reduce sycophancy while preserving updating, and still observe a persistent trade-off.

The third layer is mechanistic analysis. The authors use gradient-based attribution patching to localize components associated with answer flips, validate them with cross-patching, and estimate contrastive steering directions for each behavior. Two findings matter most. First, the components implicated in Unsupported-Yielding and Rational-Updating overlap substantially, especially in specific layers and attention heads. Second, the steering directions for the two behaviors are positively aligned rather than cleanly separable. This implies that many interventions are not selectively suppressing sycophancy; they are perturbing a more general internal mechanism for revising answers in response to second-turn signals. Motivated by this, the paper explores a preliminary orthogonalized steering procedure: remove the component aligned with rational updating before applying anti-sycophancy steering. On TruthfulQA this yields modest and model-dependent selectivity gains, particularly at the attention-head level, but it is clearly presented as an early probe rather than a finished solution.65:T57f,The experimental emphasis is on relative behavioral shifts rather than headline benchmark scores. Across four task families—truthfulness QA, factual QA, evidence verification, and math reasoning—the main pattern is stable: interventions that reduce Unsupported-Yielding usually also reduce Rational-Updating. This holds across DPO, SFT, and activation-steering style methods. In other words, the model becomes harder to push around by the user, but also less willing to revise when new evidence should change the answer.

The mechanistic section provides the strongest evidence. Figure 4 shows overlap in the components associated with the two behaviors. Figure 5 shows positive alignment between their steering directions. Cross-patching further supports that the localized components are not merely correlated with the behavior but causally involved in answer flips.

The orthogonalized-steering exploration reports modest selectivity gains on TruthfulQA. The paper is careful here: the gains are limited and model-dependent, so this should not be read as a mature mitigation recipe. The more important result is conceptual. It demonstrates that selective control may be possible, but only with finer representational disentanglement than simple suppression.

If you care about numbers, the most informative view is not raw final accuracy but paired changes in the two metrics under each intervention.66:T8dc,The core idea is to combine natural-looking text with a fully controlled latent process. The teacher is Gemma-2-2B base, paired with a pretrained Gemma Scope sparse autoencoder. From the SAE latents at an intermediate layer, the authors select 8 directions that are approximately orthogonal and weakly correlated, to avoid pre-existing semantic neighborhood structure. During generation, a ring-shaped 8-state Markov chain determines which latent is active at each token. The teacher is then steered along the corresponding SAE decoder direction by adding a scaled vector into the residual stream from layers 12 through 23.

The scaling uses the latent’s average firing magnitude and layerwise residual norms. This is not just a cosmetic detail: the paper reports that injecting at a single layer lets later layers partially undo the intervention, so persistent multi-layer steering is needed to write a durable signal into the generated text. The resulting corpus still looks like ordinary language, but token probabilities are subtly biased by the current hidden state.

A small student Transformer is then trained from scratch on this corpus, with no access to the latent labels. Analysis proceeds in two stages. First, the authors test whether the student linearly encodes the posterior belief over the hidden Markov state, not merely the last state or local lexical cues. Because the latent process is known, they can compute the ground-truth belief state from the observation history and fit linear probes against it. Second, they study the geometry of the 8 latent values themselves in the student’s representation space, using class-conditioned centers, pairwise distances, and low-dimensional projections. This distinction is central: a belief state is a distribution over latent values, while concept geometry concerns how the latent values themselves are arranged.

Relative to earlier work, the novelty is threefold: the data are natural-looking rather than fully synthetic; the paper studies belief tracking and concept geometry in the same setup; and the latent directions are deliberately chosen to be unrelated, so any recovered ring geometry is more plausibly caused by the imposed dynamics than by pre-existing semantic similarity in the teacher.67:T75c,The main empirical findings are qualitative but fairly clean. First, the student does learn belief tracking. Linear probes recover the posterior over the hidden state from internal activations, and this signal emerges progressively across layers rather than appearing only at the output. The paper also compares against simpler alternatives, such as probes based on local token information or direct state prediction, and those do not explain the results as well, suggesting the model is not merely memorizing shallow lexical patterns.

Second, the latent-state geometry is recovered. The 8 states form a ring-like arrangement in the student’s representation space, with the correct neighbor order matching the imposed Markov chain. This is important because the teacher SAE directions were selected to be approximately uncorrelated, so the ring is unlikely to be inherited from the teacher’s original semantic geometry.

Third, the control experiments matter. When the transition structure is randomized or the steering signal is weakened or removed, the ring geometry becomes much less pronounced and belief recovery degrades. The paper also compares steering strategies and finds that single-layer interventions are easier for the teacher to wash out, while multi-layer steering leaves a more learnable trace in the generated corpus.

Fourth, the authors discuss the trade-off between naturalness and learnability. If steering is too weak, the student cannot reliably infer the latent process; if it is too strong, the text distribution drifts further from ordinary language. The chosen operating point keeps the text readable while still embedding a recoverable hidden signal. The paper is more about mechanism validation than benchmark gains, so the most informative evidence is in the probe plots, geometry visualizations, and ablations rather than a single headline metric.68:T4b5,Reported results include concrete geometric statistics:
- On OLMo-2 1B and OLMoE-1B-7B (with dense OLMo-2 7B as a scale check), mean pairwise cosine similarity among foundation directions is ~0.22–0.27 across layers (positive everywhere), inconsistent with collapse.
- Compared to a matched non-moral battery, the shared positive component is ~20× larger (0.26 vs 0.013; paired Δ=0.223, CI [0.202, 0.244]).
- Effective dimensionality is ~5 at every layer for the six directions (near the maximum for mean-centered directions), indicating multi-dimensional structure.
- Clustering does not recover the MFT individualizing/binding split; the most consistent pairing is care–sanctity (crossing MFT groups), with limited statistical power for group tests.
- Dilemma compositionality: 15 two-foundation dilemma probes reach 94.2% mean accuracy; dilemma directions are partly explained by the 2D subspace of their component foundations; dilemmas sharing a foundation are closer (mean cosine 0.273 vs 0.196, permutation p=0.0001).
- Fragility: per-foundation fragility shows a uniform dense-vs-MoE gap (~2.3×) rather than foundation-specific differences; output dilution suppresses moral encoding broadly.69:T491,The production telemetry shows that 37% of get_epics calls and 28% of get_merge_request_diffs calls exceed an 8K-token budget, while the observed rate of agent-initiated second-chunk requests is zero. The structured analysis uses 4,175 Bash file-search gold-selection events extracted from the logs. The offline study runs on 500 SWE-bench Verified tasks. Candidate lists are bimodal: 57.6% of tasks have at most 5 candidates, 31.4% are near the 50-candidate cap, and 11.0% fall in between. The FIFO baseline places the gold file at rank one in about 24.2% of tasks. A downstream probe is run on 100 tasks across five language models. The main negative result is that improving p1 does not reliably improve downstream accuracy, because the binding condition is whether the gold item reaches the first chunk at all, not whether it is ranked first inside that chunk. The released pipeline is reported to reproduce on a single workstation with a 24GB GPU.6a:T557,The work extends the Gemini-based Co-Scientist system into an execution-grounded multi-agent framework spanning hypothesis generation, experiment planning, tool use, result interpretation, and manuscript drafting. The key idea is not a new foundation model, but adaptive orchestration across domains with different verification costs and safety constraints. In materials science, the system interfaces with a semi-automated CVD setup, proposes candidate recipes under lab constraints, and relies on experts to select and execute promising options. In another materials setting, Gemini 3 Deep Think is used for fast inference and direct hardware control to drive single-attempt growth of 2D semiconductors. In biology, the system works with experts who iteratively refine the task framing, while the model predicts emergent swarming phenotypes of engineered E. coli from sparse imaging data and the predictions are checked against wet-lab measurements. In computer science, the system operates autonomously from a high-level research directive to discover an inference-time scaling architecture and evaluate it on medical benchmarks. The unifying design choice is selective autonomy: the system does not insist on full automation, but allocates decision authority between AI and humans based on execution risk, observability, and the availability of reliable feedback.6b:T52e,The evidence is presented mainly as real-world case studies rather than a single standardized benchmark. In materials science, Co-Scientist proposes a non-hazardous precursor route for Ti3C2Tx MXene growth; after expert optimization and physical execution, the resulting structures show characteristics similar to Ti3C2Tx MXene, although the paper explicitly notes that further experiments are needed to confirm the atomic structure. In a second materials setup, the system uses Gemini 3 Deep Think for rapid reasoning and direct hardware control, achieving successful single-attempt growth of monolayer MoS2, MoSe2, and WS2 while adapting to lab constraints within minutes. In biology, the system predicts swarming phenotypes across IPTG concentration gradients and is quantitatively validated against unpublished wet-lab morphology measurements, with the claimed benefit of reducing combinatorial screening. In computer science, the system autonomously discovers an inference-time scaling architecture that outperforms six frontier models on HealthBench Hard and Professional and reduces potential clinical harm in blinded physician evaluation, though the excerpt does not provide the full numbers. Overall, the experimental contribution is breadth of deployment and grounding, not tightly controlled algorithmic comparison.6c:T7f3,ASIL is presented as an agent-native interaction layer rather than a single backend. The core design choice is to expose software through the deepest feasible access path available for each application. On the observation side, the agent receives a structured JSON object containing task metadata, application state, interactive elements, environment context, navigation structure, and a concise textual summary. On the action side, the agent emits a schema-constrained JSON action with explicit type, target, and parameters. The key shift is from “where to click” to “what to modify / invoke / export.”

The implementation is organized around three realization paths:
1. file-based access, where structured file formats are read and modified directly;
2. scripting-based access, where native scripting runtimes or automation APIs are used;
3. service-based access, where backend APIs or service endpoints expose semantic operations.

The paper emphasizes four design principles: completeness, semanticity, stability, and composability. Completeness addresses the partial observability of screenshots. Semanticity aligns actions with meaningful software operations. Stability avoids UI-dependent identifiers and layout drift. Composability allows complex tasks to be solved through a sequence of higher-level operations rather than long GUI event chains.

A notable systems contribution is the onboarding framework: reviewed interface profiles are compiled into validated adapter contracts. This makes ASIL more than a one-off wrapper. It resembles tool schemas or MCP-style interfaces, but with a stronger emphasis on state observability and action closure.

Importantly, ASIL is also treated as a trainable environment. The authors run small-scale SFT followed by resource- and time-limited on-policy RL. Because states and actions are structured and directly checkable, reward design and rollout efficiency become much cleaner than in screenshot-and-click settings. That is the part most relevant to agent training dynamics.6d:T689,The evaluation has three layers. First, the environment and benchmark: ASIL is instantiated across 15 applications, with 300 single-application tasks and 80 multi-application tasks. The authors also render GUI snapshots from the underlying software state at every step, so ASIL and screenshot-driven agents can be compared under the same task definitions and validators. This is an important design choice because it controls for task specification while changing only the interaction interface.

Second, the interface comparison: the abstract reports that ASIL reaches above 80 with closed models on the benchmark. The paper also includes repaired GUI / 50max results, matched native-interface baselines such as LibreOffice UNO and draw.io MCP, and independent validity checks to bound the comparison. The main empirical message is not just higher end performance, but shorter and more stable trajectories. GUI agents pay a large step budget and are fragile to grounding, focus, timing, and layout errors. ASIL compresses many multi-step GUI procedures into one or a few semantic actions.

Third, the training results: the authors run small-scale SFT plus resource-limited, time-limited on-policy RL on Qwen3.5-2B and Qwen3.5-9B, and report double-digit gains. They further confirm the trend on a curated 80-task hard suite. There is also an ablation over realization patterns, comparing file, scripting, and service access routes. Even without every number in the abstract, the important result is clear: once the interface is structured and semantic, smaller models become trainable for software operation in a way that is much harder under screenshot-based interaction.6e:T4f1,For a quick but useful read, focus on three parts. First, the introduction and the interface-mismatch section: this is where the paper makes its real argument, namely that many GUI-agent failures are caused by the wrong observation/action interface rather than insufficient reasoning alone. Second, read the ASIL interface definition and realization methodology carefully, especially the observation/action schema, the three access paths, and the four design principles. That tells you whether the proposal is generalizable or just engineering around a few apps. Third, inspect the benchmark construction and the comparison protocol: shared validators, GUI rendering from state, native-interface baselines, and the hard-suite training results are the places where the paper either earns or loses credibility.

A practical reading order is: problem framing → interface design → benchmark construction → training experiments. In about 30–45 minutes, that should be enough to capture the main idea. The two deeper questions worth thinking about are: how much of the gain comes from better tool interfaces versus better state representations, and whether ASIL-like environments could become a source of continual pretraining or RL curricula for software agents.6f:T792,GRAIN has three main components. First, it uses an explicit pipeline. Rather than letting the model mix extraction, graph construction, and computation inside unconstrained chain-of-thought, the task is decomposed into semantic parsing of the graph and task arguments, followed by tool execution with the appropriate graph algorithm. The motivation is straightforward: shortest path, matching, coloring, and related computations are deterministic; the real weakness of LLMs is the language-to-structure mapping.

Second, the method enforces structural invariance during training. The authors construct multiple isomorphic views of the same underlying graph: node identifiers may be random, semantic, aliased, or noisy, and the task description may range from standardized templates to more realistic narratives. The model is trained to recover the same intermediate graph despite these surface changes. This is more than ordinary augmentation, because the reward directly checks whether the predicted intermediate graph matches the ground-truth topology. That gives denser and more targeted feedback than final-answer supervision alone.

Third, GRAIN uses single-agent RL as a form of robustness distillation. The goal is not to build a multi-agent system, but to absorb into one model the robustness that would otherwise require repeated decomposition and verification across multiple agents. The RL objective jointly rewards correct structure recovery and correct tool invocation. The intended effect is to learn identifier-invariant and formulation-invariant parsing rules instead of memorizing templates.

The accompanying benchmark, GRIT, is also a substantial part of the contribution. It covers six graph problems across 31 real-world prototypes, with controlled multi-view variants for naming and narrative style. That makes it possible to separate failures of structure extraction from failures of downstream algorithmic solving.70:T6da,The experiments are built around robustness diagnosis rather than a single leaderboard number. The first result is that the robustness gap is real: under identifier shift and task-form shift, performance varies significantly even when the underlying graph is unchanged. Closed models tend to retain stronger average accuracy but still show unstable variance across naming schemes. Open models degrade much more sharply under non-canonical identifiers and realistic narratives. This is an important finding because it shows that strong performance on sanitized graph benchmarks does not imply reliable real-world graph reasoning.

Against baselines, GRAIN is reported to outperform standard CoT, SFT, and more expensive multi-agent approaches in out-of-distribution robustness while keeping latency and token cost lower. The most informative results are likely the breakdowns by naming scheme, narrative type, graph size, and task complexity. If the gains are consistent across those slices, that supports the claim that the reward is improving the language-to-structure stage rather than exploiting a narrow template.

A key ablation concerns the structural reward itself. The paper argues that rewarding intermediate graph correctness is better than rewarding only the final answer, and better than static supervision alone. The reason is intuitive: final-answer rewards are sparse and can be accidentally correct even when parsing is wrong, while structural rewards directly supervise semantic parsing quality. Although the abstract does not list all numbers, the central empirical message is that GRAIN yields more stable performance under surface perturbations and converts part of the robustness of complex multi-agent pipelines into a single model.71:T49e,A good skim has three stops. First, read the introduction and the GRIT setup carefully to understand what is actually being evaluated: not generic text-serialized graph reasoning, but robustness of language-to-graph extraction under naming and formulation shifts. Without that framing, the paper is easy to misread as just another graph benchmark. Second, read the method section with attention to the semantic parsing → tool execution pipeline and the definition of the structure invariance reward. In particular, check how the predicted graph is matched against the ground-truth topology, whether graph isomorphism is handled explicitly, and how node renaming is treated. Third, inspect the OOD splits and the ablations comparing CoT, SFT, RL, and multi-agent baselines.

If the goal is only to capture the main idea, 20–30 minutes should be enough. The deeper follow-up questions are more interesting: whether this kind of verifiable intermediate-structure RL can transfer to code dependency graphs, knowledge graph extraction, or tool-planning graphs, and whether invariance rewards could be connected to pretraining-time augmentation, canonicalization, or schema induction.72:T465,ContextPilot expands the context-management action space and changes the RL procedure. On the tool side, it adds planning, long-term memory, and soft context offloading beyond search, deletion, and summarization. Planning gives the agent a global structure before later actions. Long-term memory stores scattered evidence in a reusable form. Soft offloading acts as adaptive compression or temporary externalization rather than hard deletion. On the training side, the paper introduces context-aware partial rollout. It identifies influential context-management actions using changes in context and policy entropy, then branches rollouts around these critical actions instead of exploring every action uniformly. For credit assignment, it estimates the advantage of an intermediate context-management action using rewards from subsequent branches. This gives a finer signal than assigning the final trajectory reward to every step. optimizat","starred":false,"priority":"p2","reading_tier":"must_read","source":"arxiv","sources":["arxiv"],"published_at":"","category_id":"llm_pretrain","cover_url":"/covers/2608_26288.png","hf_upvotes":0,"arxiv_categories":["cs.LG","math.OC","stat.ML"],"summary":{"core_problem":"这篇论文解决 预训练优化器研究有直接价值。Muon 已经在大规模预训练中表现出竞争力，核心操作是对矩阵参数的 momentum 做近似正交化。理论上，exact polar map 在奇异值接近 0 或秩变化处不连续，对应到 online learning 视角会退化为 operator-norm ball 上的 follow-the-leader，可能产生线性 regret，无法保证非光滑目标的 stationarity 保证。对矩阵参数来说，Muon 的理想方向是 momentum 矩阵 M 的 polar factor：若 M = U Sigma V^T，则更新方向为 U V^T，相当于保留奇异向量、把所有正奇异值映射到 1。问题在于 exact polar map 是不连续的。有限 Newton–Schulz 使用固定奇多项式迭代，只需要矩阵乘法，不做 SVD；截断在 q 步后得到的映射不再是硬阈值式 polar factor，而是对奇异值施加一个平滑函数。论文把这一有限迭代表示为一个 smoothed spectral potential 的梯度，即 update direction = grad Phi_q(M)，其中 Phi_q 作用在奇异值上。这样 Muon update 可以被看成 gradient-based prediction algorithm。regret 分解为两项：penalty term 衡量平滑势函数和 nuclear norm 的距离，q 越大越小；stability term 由诱导映射的 Lipschitz 常数控制，q 越大通常越大。选择 q = O(log(1/epsilon)) 可以平衡两项，让有限 Newton–Schulz 足够接近 polar，又保持可控平滑性。这个分析和把有限迭代当 approximation error 的思路不同：它不是证明“有限步足够像 exact polar”，而是利用“有限步不像 exact polar 的地方”来获得稳定性。","experiments":"论文主要是理论结果，不以大规模预训练实验为核心。设目标函数 Lipschitz、可非光滑且非凸；随机梯度 oracle 无偏且噪声有界。对任意半径 rho > 0 和精度 epsilon > Practical Muon uses a finite number of Newton–Schulz iterations to approximately orthogonalize matrix-valued momentum, but existing analyses either replace this loop with the exact polar factor or treat finite depth as approximation error. The paper shows that, for nonsmooth nonconvex optimization, finite Newton–Schulz can be the mechanism that enables convergence.","importance":"This is directly relevant to LLM pretraining optimization. Muon is attractive because most LLM parameters are matrices and its matrix-momentum orthogonalization can improve update geometry at scale. The theoretical issue is that the exact polar map is discontinuous and, under the online-learning view, exact-polar Muon behaves like follow-the-leader over the operator-norm ball, which can incur linear regret. The paper explains why the implementation detail used in practice—truncating Newton–Schulz after a few matrix-multiply steps—can improve the optimization theory by smoothing the polar map. The contribution is not a new pretraining recipe; it is a sharper explanation of why the practical optimizer may have better stability properties than its exact-polar idealization.","technical_approach":"$17","experiments":"The paper is primarily theoretical. Under a Lipschitz objective that may be nonsmooth and nonconvex, with an unbiased stochastic gradient oracle and bounded noise, Muon with momentum and q = O(log(1/epsilon)) Newton–Schulz steps per round finds a (rho, epsilon)-stationary point in expectation using O(rho^{-1} epsilon^{-3} + epsilon^{-2}) stochastic gradient evaluations. The stationarity notion follows Jiang et al. 2026a. The leading rho^{-1} epsilon^{-3} term matches the guarantees reported for Pion and Leon under the same criterion, while staying closer to the Muon update used in practice because it does not add stochastic perturbations or augment the momentum matrix. The paper also contrasts this with exact-polar Muon, which can fail to converge in the same framework because its corresponding online learner can suffer linear regret.","reading_guide":"Read carefully. pre","starred":false,"priority":"p2","reading_tier":"skim","source":"arxiv","sources":["arxiv"],"published_at":"","category_id":"efficient","cover_url":"/covers/2608_27128.png","hf_upvotes":0,"arxiv_categories":["cs.CL"],"summary":{"core_problem":"这篇工作处理的是长上下文推理里的一个老问题：KV 的重要性定义成“唯一性”的反面：如果某个 token 的 key 在上下文其他非相邻位置存在近重复，那么删掉它后，模型仍可能通过保留下来的近重复项恢复这部分信息；如果没有重复，它更可能是不可替代的。具体做法是：对每个 token 的 key，统计有多少其他非相邻 token 与它的 key cosine similarity 超过阈值，这个 twin count 越高，说明冗余越强，重要性越低。这里有两个设计点值得注意。第一，使用 key 而不是 value 或 hidden state，是因为 eviction 决策发生在 attention 检索层面，key 更直接反映“可被匹配到的记忆地址”；第二，排除相邻 token，是为了避免把局部连续文本的平凡相似性误判成真正的语义冗余。\n\n更有意思的是它不是 standalone policy，而是 repair pass。给定任意已有 eviction 方法输出的 retained set 和 evicted set，TwinKV 检查两类错误：一类是某个被删 token 在 retained set 中没有近重复，属于 unrecoverable eviction；另一类是某个被留 token 在 retained set 内有冗余副本，属于 wasted retention。然后在不改变总预算的前提下做 swap：把前者换回，把后者换出。这样做的好处是，它不需要知道被包装方法内部如何打分，也不需要重新排序全体 token，只利用最终保留结果做局部修正。论文还专门把这种 pairwise redundancy 与 anchor-based 方法区分开：后者用单一全局参考点衡量“离群程度”，更像异常检测；TwinKV Our analysis shows","starred":false,"priority":"p3","reading_tier":"skim","source":"arxiv","sources":["arxiv"],"published_at":"","category_id":"efficient","cover_url":"/covers/2608_26581.png","hf_upvotes":0,"arxiv_categories":["cs.LG"],"summary":{"core_problem":"这篇工作研究的是多模态大模型在超低比特量化，尤其是 FP4 训练/部署时，为什么会明显失稳，以及怎样在不回退到高精度、不改模型结构的前提下，把主要误差源压住。论文的核心判断很明确：在代表性的 MLLM 里，4-bit 退化的主因不是权重量化，而是激活量化；更具体地说，是某些模块里重尾分布和离群值导致的激活失真。作者要解决的是这个训练期动态出现、且模块依赖很强的 activation outlier 问题。","importance":"对基座研究的价值不在于“又一个量化技巧”，而在于它把多模态统一模型里的数值脆弱性拆得比较清楚。第一，论文给出一个对 MLLM 很实用的结论：视觉侧通常比语言侧更怕超低比特，且不同架构的脆弱模块并不相同，因此不能直接套文本 LLM 的统一量化 recipe。第二，它把关注点从权重转向激活，这对训练系统、低精度预训练、以及未来 native multimodal pretrain 的硬件友好设计都有启发。第三，提出的 RFQ 属于一种训练感知的误差补偿思路：不是试图完全消灭 outlier，而是显式编码量化残差。这种思路对更广义的低精度训练也有参考价值。","technical_approach":"论文先做系统性诊断，再给出方法。诊断部分覆盖两类代表性 MLLM：Wan2.2 这类多模态生成模型，以及 Qwen3-VL 这类多模态推理模型；量化格式包括 MXFP8、MXFP4、HiF4，并且不是只量化某一层，而是覆盖视觉编码器、文本编码器、注意力、MLP、多模态投影层、MoE 等关键组件。作者通过模块级 ablation 发现，FP8 基本接近无损，但 FP4 的退化高度异质：Wan2.2 中视觉生成主干更脆弱，文本编码器相对稳；Qwen3-VL 中视觉编码器最敏感，但语言主干也会出现明显退化。进一步拆分 weight-only 与 activation quantization 后，结论是激活量化贡献了主要性能损失。\n\n在此基础上，作者提出 Residual Fallback Quantization, RFQ。它不是常见的 threshold-based outlier fallback：后者通常会检测大值并把少量 outlier 保留在高精度或单独路径里，这在训练和硬件实现上都比较麻烦，也容易引入离散选择。RFQ 的做法更连续：先把激活做主路径量化，得到一个 FP4 表示；再显式计算量化残差，并把这个残差通过第二条低比特路径再量化一次，用于重构。也就是说，输出近似是 q(x) + q_res(x - q(x))，而不是“普通值走低比特，离群值走高比特”。这样做有几个好处：\n\n1. 全流程可微，适合端到端训练；\n2. 不需要阈值选择，避免不同模块、不同训练阶段阈值难调；\n3. 不依赖 full-precision fallback，保持 FP4 友好；\n4. 更适合处理训练中动态变化的 outlier，因为它补偿的是当前量化误差，而不是依赖静态校准统计。\n\n从方法定位看，RFQ 介于 PTQ 的静态平滑和 QAT 的显式混精度回退之间。它承认 FP4 无法完整容纳激活动态范围，因此直接对误差建模，而不是强行把原分布压进单一路径量化器里。","experiments":"从已给出的全文内容可以明确读到几类关键结果。\n\n1. 精度格式对性能影响分层明显：MXFP8 基本接近无损，而 MXFP4/HiF4 会带来显著退化。这说明 8-bit 在当前 MLLM 上已经比较成熟，真正困难的是 4-bit 端到端训练。\n2. 退化来源上，activation quantization 明显重于 weight quantization。作者做了大量消融来区分两者贡献，结论是只压权重通常还能接受，一旦把激活也压到 FP4，性能会明显下滑。\n3. 模块敏感性高度异质。Wan2.2 的 WanDiT 视觉生成主干是主要瓶颈，UMT5 文本编码器相对稳；Qwen3-VL 的视觉编码器最敏感，但语言模块也不是完全安全区。这说明“统一全模型同一量化策略”在 MLLM 上往往不够好。\n4. RFQ 能在不使用高精度回退的情况下恢复一部分 FP4 损失。摘要里没有给出具体百分点，但从叙述看，作者强调 RFQ 主要改善的是由激活 outlier 引起的训练不稳定和精度塌陷，而不是对所有模块平均小修小补。\n\n如果正文表格提供了任务指标，建议重点看两类数字：一是 FP8、FP4、HiF4 在生成与推理任务上的相对差距；二是 weight-only、act-only、W+A 量化的拆分结果。对预训练研究者来说，这比最终单一 benchmark 分数更有信息量，因为它直接告诉你误差预算该花在哪一侧。","reading_guide":"这篇适合按“诊断优先，方法其次”的顺序读。先看实验设计和模块级 ablation，再看 RFQ 细节。具体建议如下。\n\n第一，先读引言和实验总表，确认作者研究的不是单一模型或单一任务，而是生成型与推理型两类 MLLM。这样后面看到模块差异时更容易判断哪些结论可迁移。\n\n第二，重点看 activation vs weight 的拆分实验，以及各模块的敏感性排序。这里是全文最有信息密度的部分，因为它回答了“为什么 FP4 不行”而不是只展示“FP4 结果差”。\n\n第三，再看 RFQ 的公式和实现细节，尤其是残差如何量化、是否引入额外存储/带宽、训练时和推理时的开销如何。若你关心低精度预训练，这部分要结合系统代价一起读，而不是只看精度恢复。\n\n第四，若正文有激活分布图、离群值统计、不同层的误差热图，建议细看。这些图通常比最终 benchmark 更能说明问题。\n\n作为 skim 论文，泛读 30 到 45 分钟可以抓住主线；若你正在做 FP8/FP4 训练、视觉 tokenizer、或 unified multimodal pretrain 的系统优化，建议花 1 到 1.5 小时把消融和附录实现细节读完。","authors_note":""},"summary_en":{"core_problem":"The paper studies why multimodal LLMs become fragile under ultra-low-bit quantization, especially FP4, and how to recover performance without reverting to higher precision or changing the model architecture. The paper addresses: how to refine hardware-valid per-group scales in a lightweight, post-processing PTQ step, with zero inference-time overhead.","importance":"Primarily an inference/PTQ contribution, but it matters to foundation-model practitioners because NVFP4 is likely to become a common deployment target and shifts the bottleneck toward scale calibration. Optimizing discrete per-group scales under full G would couple channels and make the search combinatorial. The method uses a diagonal approximation diag(G), yielding per-input-channel energy weights h_j that still capture which channels matter most.\n\nAlgorithmically, it starts from a baseline NVFP4 scale per group (typically max-abs then snapped to an E4M3-representable FP8 scale). proof-state-tree，把粗粒度证明步骤表示成状态转移，每个转移对应一个局部推理责任。这样做的目的，是把“这一步大概有问题”变成“这个状态过渡需要证明什么”。第二段从可疑转移中抽取 typed proof obligations。这里的 typed 指 obligation 不是统一的一类命题，而是区分代数变形、蕴含传递、存在性构造、边界条件、分类讨论衔接等不同责任类型，再分别走轻量检查和 Lean 验证。Lean 不是直接裁判整步，而是作为结构化证据源：只有当自动形式化得到的 formal statement 与原始 obligation 语义足够一致时，Lean 结果才被采纳。为此论文设计 semantic alignment score，用来衡量 formal target 是否保留了原始自然语言断言的条件、方向、量词和结论强度，避免出现“形式上可证，但不是原句意思”的 drifted target。第三段 synthesis 把多个局部证据回聚到原始 step 级别，输出 first erroneous step。这里的关键不是简单投票，而是优先利用能直接指向最早失效转移的高置信证据。整体上，FaithSieve 的新意不在某个单一模块，而在于把 关系。这里的关键不是单次 LLM judge，而是把 LLM 放在离线图构造环节，用来做候选验证和结构化抽取，而不是直接拿它生成 benchmark 后就结束。\n\n有了 verified conflict edge 之后，作者从冲突子图里采样，合成 QA：一个问题 q 对应一个答案集合 A={v1,...,vk}，其中 k≥2，每个答案都必须能追溯到源文档，并且还要经过外部公开权威来源验证与人工复核。这样得到的不是“模型在给定证据下如何整合冲突”，而是“不给证据时，模型参数里到底保留了哪些 account”。\n\n评测指标也做了拆分。论文不是只算一个 accuracy，而是区分 fact recall 与 account completeness：前者看模型是否至少记住了这个低曝光事实的一种说法，后者看它是否把所有已验证 account 都说出来。这个拆分很重要，因为很多模型并不是完全不知道，而是只记住了曝光更高的一边。论文后面还把每个 account 在语料中的支持文档数作为 exposure proxy，分析不同侧的文档频次与 recall / completeness 的关系。这一点让 benchmark 不只是排名工具，而能回到训练数据分布本身。","experiments":"基准规模是 1,094 个闭卷问题，来自低曝光网页语料中的自然分歧案例。每个样本都经过源文档追溯、外部验证和人工审核。作者评测了 32 个模型。最强模型也只能在 52.4% 的问题上同时找回两个 account；而在几乎所有剩余失败样本里，模型并不是完全答不出，而是能答出其中一个 account，却漏掉另一个。这说明主要失败模式不是“事实完全遗忘”，而是“记忆不完整”。\n\n论文最有信息量的实验不是单纯模型排名，而是 exposure asymmetry 分析。作者统计冲突两侧各自被多少文档支持，用支持文档数近似训练曝光度。结果显示：更常见 account 的曝光与 fact recall 更相关，也就是它决定模型是否能把这个事实想起来；较少见 account 的曝光则更影响 completeness，也就是模型能否把另一种已验证说法也保留下来。这个结果和预训练里常见的频次偏置一致，但这里给出了更细粒度的闭卷证据。\n\n从摘要和正文可见，作者还强调 benchmark construction 的效率：通过 knowledge-point clustering 和 entity-based retrieval，把原本需要大规模 pairwise LLM can an LLM recover all of them from parametric memory in a closed-book setting? Existing long-tail QA benchmarks mostly assume a single canonical answer, so they only test whether a model recalls a rare fact at all. Existing conflict benchmarks usually provide conflicting passages at inference time, so they test evidence integration rather than stored knowledge. ElephantBench is built to isolate memory completeness: does the model remember the fact, and if yes, does it retain the full set of verified accounts or only the dominant one?","importance":"This matters for pretraining because it exposes a failure mode that ordinary accuracy hides. A trace can be semantically correct while still being difficult for the current policy to learn from because it lies outside the policy’s native distribution. This matters for synthetic CoT data, tool-use trace distillation, and multimodal reasoning supervision. For pretraining-oriented work, the useful abstraction is that supervision quality includes both semantic quality and distributional learnability.","technical_approach":"Echo-GRPO rewrites privileged teacher traces into the student model’s own idiolect before using them in GRPO. The goal is not to copy the teacher’s wording, but to preserve the teacher’s reasoning semantics using tokens that the student policy is more likely to produce. The key component is Dual-Reference Decoding. It combines two conditional distributions from the initial policy in a product-of-experts form. The semantic reference keeps the paraphrase faithful to the privileged trace. The distributional reference keeps each generated token probable under the student. The resulting trace remains close to the teacher in meaning but closer to the student in probability space. When optimized with GRPO, these rewritten traces are less likely to be clipped, so semantically important reasoning tokens can contribute gradients. The same paraphrasing module is also presented as a plug-in preprocessing step for SFT and other distillation pipelines.","experiments":"The experiments target video reasoning distillation. The trained model family is called VideoEcho-R1. The paper evaluates three multimodal backbones: InternVL3.5-4B, Qwen3-VL-4B, and Qwen3-VL-8B, across five video reasoning benchmarks. Baselines include vanilla GRPO, SFT, and Mixed-Policy GRPO. Echo-GRPO shows consistent gains across the tested backbones and benchmarks. The more informative evidence is the token-level analysis: original privileged traces contain many low-likelihood tokens under the student, which leads to large importance-ratio deviations and clipping; after idiolectal paraphrasing, the traces move closer to the student distribution and retain more useful gradients on reasoning tokens. ","starred":false,"priority":"p3","reading_tier":"skim","source":"arxiv","sources":["arxiv"],"published_at":"","category_id":"post_train","cover_url":"/covers/2608_26956.png","hf_upvotes":0,"arxiv_categories":["cs.CV"],"summary":{"core_problem":"这篇工作解决的是视觉生成对齐里的 试图把“评价标准本身”也变成模型输出的一部分，先为当前输入动态生成 rubric，再按 rubric 对候选图像做分维度打分和偏好判断。","importance":"对基座预训练的直接关系不如训练 recipe 或 tokenizer 那么近，但它对 post-train 信号质量很有参考价值。reward model 决定了后续 RL 或 preference optimization 学到什么，而这篇工作的核心启发是：奖励不一定非得压成一个不可解释的标量，也可以先显式生成任务相关的评价协议，再据此打分。这个思路对多模态对齐、可解释 verifier、以及高质量合成偏好数据都有意义。尤其在图像生成和编辑里，固定维度 reward 往往把不同任务混成同一种偏好函数，RubricRM 则尝试让 reward 随输入条件化。若把这个想法迁移到语言模型，类似机制可以用于动态 rubric 的 reasoning/verifier、代码评测维度分解、或多约束指令跟随的 reward 建模。","technical_approach":"方法上，RubricRM 是一个 pairwise generative reward model。输入是指令 q 和两个候选图像 I_A、I_B；编辑任务还包含源图像。模型不是直接输出 A/B 偏好，而是一次性生成一套结构化 rubric，并给两个候选图像分别做分维度评分。rubric 包含四部分：任务意图、原子评价维度 d_i、各维度权重 w_i，以及每个维度的分级评分标准 L_i。随后模型给出每张图在每个维度上的分数 s_i^k，最后按加权和得到总分并决定偏好。\n\n这里的关键不是“让模型写解释”，而是把解释结构化成可执行的评分协议。相比只生成自由文本 rationale，这种设计更容易约束输出格式，也更容易把训练目标落到 dimension-level accuracy 上。\n\n训练分两阶段。第一阶段是 SFT，目标是让模型学会 rubric trajectory，也就是从输入到意图拆解、维度生成、权重分配、评分标准，再到候选图像评分的整条推理轨迹。训练监督来自 teacher-synthesized rubric trajectories。第二阶段是 RL，文中使用 dimension-level GRPO。它不是只看最终 A/B 是否判对，而是对每个维度上的预测分差与参考分差进行对齐；若偏好方向判反，则施加更强惩罚。这个设计说明作者关心的不只是最终 pairwise accuracy，而是希望模型内部的维度级判断也尽量正确。\n\n数据构建是这篇工作的另一个重点。作者认为动态 rubric 学习需要足够广的指令覆盖，否则模型会学到偏置的 rubric 模板，泛化会差。为此他们汇总多个开源 preference dataset，分析 text-to-image 和 image editing 的指令类型，设计分类标准，并用 DeepSeek-V3.2 做自动类别标注。然后基于类别分布做 balanced sampling，找出低覆盖类别，再为这些类别合成补充 prompt、生成候选图像并收集专家偏好标注。最后再为每个 preference sample 合成 rubric trajectory，得到 31.8K 的生成训练样本和 30.7K 的编辑训练样本。这个流程说明他们把 reward model 训练看成“数据覆盖 + 结构化监督 + 偏好优化”的组合问题，而不是单纯换个 loss。","experiments":"实验上，作者分别在 Standard OPSD assumes that a privileged teacher, conditioned on both the problem and a reference solution, is always the right token-level target along the student's rollout. The authors argue that this assumption is too strong. Access to a reference does not guarantee that the teacher's local next-token preferences are optimal for a deployment-time student that only sees the problem. In extraction, a reference corpus is passed through both the base model and the finetuned model, and the method records the logit difference for each next-token prediction. The key design choice is to compare two related checkpoints rather than interpret a single model in isolation. In aggregation, the paper proposes two simple mechanisms. Top-K aggregation counts which tokens repeatedly appear among the largest positive logit shifts, producing a ranked list of amplified tokens. NMF aggregation applies non-negative matrix factorization to the logit-difference matrix, yielding multiple components that can separate distinct finetuning domains. Compared with representation-level diffing, this requires only logits and is easier to run. Compared with black-box behavioral probing, it does not require knowing in advance which scenarios will trigger the hidden behavior.","experiments":"The paper evaluates Diff Mining on the hidden-objective benchmark and interpretability-agent setup from Minder et al. 2026. similar answer revisions that arise from different causes. One is Unsupported-Yielding: the model abandons its original answer under user pushback even though no new evidence is provided. The other is Rational-Updating: the model revises its answer because the second turn contains genuinely useful supporting evidence. Existing anti-sycophancy work mostly targets the former and implicitly treats fewer answer changes as better behavior. The full paper shows that this is incomplete: interventions that suppress unsupported flips often also damage the model’s ability to update when new evidence is actually informative. The central question is therefore how to distinguish these two behaviors and why current anti-sycophancy methods tend to hurt both.","importance":"$63","technical_approach":"$64","experiments":"$65","reading_guide":"Start with the task definition. That has implications for training data formats, state-supervision objectives, tool-use traces, and the practical limits of long-context reliance.","technical_approach":"SKILL.state reformulates procedural skill execution as a state-transition process. At step t, the model receives only the immutable skill specification P, the current structured state Σt, and the latest observation Ot. The model may generate within-step chain-of-thought Rt, but that reasoning is used only to produce a structured state update ΔΣt and an action at. After validation, the runtime applies the update and discards the reasoning trace. Future prompts never include previous observations, previous actions, or previous reasoning. This differs from memory or summarization systems because the execution semantics are state-centric rather than transcript-centric. The state schema is domain-level and reusable; for example, the InterCode CTF setup uses one five-field schema across 100 challenge instances.","experiments":"The evaluation uses SkillExecBench, InterCode CTF, and Sierra τ-Bench. Compared with history-based and compression-based baselines, it reduces token growth and maintains or improves task performance across multiple model families.
